solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Allowed to hold outrageous dance?

indicators.note: to hold means one piece clasps the other within it

parts.note: allowed means permitted, gave leave
OTT, over the top, means outrageous

explanation.surface: Someone was permitted to stage a shocking dance.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT (over the top) is British slang for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A gavotte is an old French court dance, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Fall in warehouse

definitions.meaning: to fall is to drop to the ground
in South and East Asia a storage depot for goods is called by this term

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to drop down, and a godown is an Asian term for a storehouse.

clue.text: Seaman in base? It's feasible

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the word for base

parts.note: base means low and vile
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sailor at a naval base makes something workable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something viable is workable and capable of succeeding.

clue.text: Trip with mates, I suspect, can demonstrate camaraderie

indicators.note: suspect suggests the letters are dubious and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday with friends is said to foster fellowship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like the speaker's verb, but it signals an anagram of TRIP MATES I.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit is the comradely feeling among members of a group, a synonym of camaraderie.

clue.text: Manuel Garcia's a composer

indicators.note: the apostrophe s stands for has, so these words contain the answer

explanation.surface: A man named Manuel Garcia is said to write music.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer is hidden across manuEL GARcia.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was an English composer, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Prime piece of pork, including stuffing

indicators.note: prime means first, so the first letter of pork is taken

parts.note: including means adding something in

explanation.surface: A choice cut of pork is served with its stuffing.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding is material used to fill or stuff something, a synonym of stuffing.

clue.text: Voracious shark splintered bargepole

indicators.note: splintered means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hungry shark smashes a long pole used on a barge.
explanation.definitionFit: The porbeagle is a large predatory mackerel shark of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Socialite, last to meet obligation

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young society woman

indicators.note: last to means the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A society girl finally honours what she owes.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is something owed, an obligation to pay.

clue.text: I misinterpreted endless inaction

indicators.note: misinterpreted means read wrongly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to misunderstanding endless laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is doing nothing, a synonym of inaction.

clue.text: Celebrated English clown, gloomy, laid off

parts.note: grim means gloomy

indicators.note: off means wrong or unsound, so the letters of laid are rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous clown, depressed, has lost his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of LAID, giving ALDI. Joseph Grimaldi was a famous Regency-era English clown.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Grimaldi was the most famous English clown, the model for the pantomime clown.

clue.text: Play with tot by front of arcade

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of arcade is taken

explanation.surface: A child plays near the entrance to an amusement arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child but is a small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage, a synonym.

clue.text: A loose blouse, Georgia's blue one

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
blue means risque or ribald
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Describes a loose top as Georgia's sad one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' suggests sad or a colour, but here means smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: A garibaldi is a loose blouse modelled on the red shirts of Garibaldi's soldiers.

clue.text: Film everyone in wide thoroughfare

indicators.note: in places one piece within the others

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
a street is a thoroughfare
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone appears in a film set on a broad avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street is a 1987 film by Oliver Stone, an example of a film.

clue.text: Indian's home, Central America

parts.note: in means at home
CA is the abbreviation for Central America

explanation.surface: Says an Indian person lives in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' here means a member of the native people of Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were a South American Indian people of the Andes.

clue.text: Filming away from the studio, love scene around noon

indicators.note: around means the pieces encircle the letter for noon

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
a scene is a location or setting

explanation.surface: A romantic scene is shot around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Filming on location means shooting at a real site rather than in a studio.

clue.text: Treated with contempt about newspaper, one in disarray

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the others

parts.note: dissed is slang for treated with disrespect
an organ is a newspaper or journal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone scorned over a newspaper is thrown into confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorganised means lacking order, a synonym of in disarray.

clue.text: Anthelion reformed at once

indicators.note: reformed means made again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A halo opposite the sun immediately takes new shape.
explanation.walkthrough: An anthelion is a bright spot in the sky opposite the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: On the nail is an idiom for immediately, especially of paying, synonymous with at once.

clue.text: Removal, or dismissal — opener must be out

indicators.note: the opener, the first letter, is to be removed

parts.note: a rejection is a dismissal

explanation.surface: Sounds like a cricket captain sacking an opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener must be out' has a cricket flavour but removes the first letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejection is the act of throwing out, a synonym of removal.

clue.text: Resident, with penny in account, worried

indicators.note: in places the penny within the letters of account
worried means shaken about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A householder frets about a penny in the bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant lives in a place, a synonym of resident.

clue.text: Provider of childish amusement, card giving evidence?

parts.note: a jack is a playing card
a witness gives evidence in the witness box

explanation.surface: A joker in court testifies, amusing the children.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts witnesses give evidence from the witness box.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a toy whose figure springs out to amuse children.

clue.text: Handsome youth from Northern Ireland's giving support to a function

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes below the others

parts.note: a do is a party or function
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: A good-looking Belfast lad helps out at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was a beautiful youth of Greek myth, so his name means a handsome young man.

clue.text: Steal from boy a novel

parts.note: to rob is to steal from
Roy is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A thief takes a book from a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Rob Roy is a novel by Sir Walter Scott, an example of a novel.

clue.text: Blockhead losing pawn, leading to mate

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped

parts.note: a chump is a fool, a blockhead
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess dunce loses a pawn and gets checkmated.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'mate' look like checkmate, but it means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum is a friend, a synonym of mate.

clue.text: Drive with crack on surface

parts.note: to surface is to rise, get up
and means with, along with
a crack is an attempt, a go

explanation.surface: Driving with a crack in the road surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places 'with crack' after 'surface' in an across answer; 'surface' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is energy and enthusiasm, the same as drive.

clue.text: Knock over raised object

parts.note: up means raised
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Someone topples a lifted item.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend is to turn upside down, to knock over.

clue.text: Welsh clergyman and poet over in Surrey (Dorking)

indicators.note: over in a down answer means the letters run upwards
in means the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: A Welsh vicar-poet turns up in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in surREY Dorking is REYD, which read upward gives the answer. Dorking is a town in Surrey, a county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dyer was an eighteenth-century Welsh clergyman and poet who wrote Grongar Hill.

clue.text: In New York, seen wearing a suit, no matter what

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: seen wearing means one piece is clothed by the other

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a case

explanation.surface: In New York someone is spotted in a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' suggests clothing but means a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: In any case is an idiom meaning whatever happens, no matter what.

clue.text: Victor letting drop wife's secret

indicators.note: letting drop means a letter is removed

parts.note: a victor is a winner
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Victor accidentally reveals his wife's secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a man's name but means one who wins.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones, so inner can mean secret.

clue.text: Turning brown, Russian river, as is to be expected

indicators.note: turning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: tan is a brown colour
the Ural is a river in Russia

explanation.surface: A Russian river turns brown, unsurprisingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means normal and in accordance with what one would expect.

clue.text: Runs out of empty and unpleasant house

indicators.note: out of means the letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: dry means empty, as a dry well
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: Someone escapes an empty and horrible house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' means a royal family line, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a ruling family line, as in the House of Windsor.
